optimizedContext.value:
# Project Configuration (specd.yaml)

Single shared project-level config for every specd tool: schema selection, workspace layout, storage paths, per-artifact constraints, plugins. CLI, MCP, plugins derive wiring from it.

## Rules

### Discovery
- Strategy order: (1) `--config <path>` = single explicit entrypoint, resolve that file + only its own `extends` chain, normal discovery MUST NOT add layers; (2) walk up from CWD, stop at first dir holding any candidate OR VCS root (`.git/`, `.hg/`, `.svn/`, or per active VCS adapter), whichever first, error if none found at/before it; (3) no VCS ancestor → CWD only, no further walk.
- Never search above VCS root (blocks parent-repo leakage in nested/sibling monorepos).
- Candidates in selected dir, ordered: `specd.yaml` → `specd.*.yaml` ascending alpha → `specd.local.yaml` → `specd.local.*.yaml` ascending alpha.
- Hosts MAY accept explicit discovery root instead of process CWD → same strategy from supplied dir. Discovery-root mode stays distinct from `--config`, which always means forced-file bootstrap, never root selector.
- Some command families MAY define bootstrap mode running without project config; `--config` meaning unchanged.
- File without `extends` = standalone root from that point.

### Privacy
- Optional `privacy` section. `mode` MUST be `hash|mask|anonymous`; `salt` optional (HMAC, recommended via env); `excludeActors` optional names/emails, default `["specd", "system@getspecd.dev"]`; `allowedMetadataKeys` optional whitelist preserved under privacy modes.

### Environment overrides
- `SPECD_ACTOR_PROVIDER` → `actorProvider`; `SPECD_PRIVACY_SALT` → `privacy.salt`; `SPECD_PRIVACY_MODE` → `privacy.mode`.
- Env vars (incl. `.env`, `.env.local`) take precedence over `specd.yaml` and `specd.local.yaml`.

### Forced actor provider
- Optional root `actorProvider` (string) forces named provider from kernel registry, bypassing auto-detection.

### Local override & cascade
- Later active layers merge over earlier: scalars last-layer-wins, objects deep-merge by key, arrays append unless entry removed via `remove`.
- `specd.local.yaml` backward-compatible: no `extends` → independent root, `specd.yaml` NOT inherited; `extends: true` → inherits previous active layer.
- Local variants ordered by filename, last wins: `specd.local.10-team.yaml` → `specd.local.20-machine.yaml` → `specd.local.99-final.yaml`.
- `specd init` MUST add `specd.local.yaml` + `specd.local.*.yaml` to `.gitignore`.

### Cascade identity & removal model
- `extends` has exactly two valid forms: `true` (inherit previous active layer) or `<path>` (inherit one explicit file that MUST already belong to same applicable chain, else discovered file ignored during normal discovery).
- `extends: <path>` allows discoverable-but-inactive files: `specd.local.experimental.yaml` stays inactive unless `specd.experimental.yaml` is already active or selected via `--config`.
- `remove` valid ONLY in configs declaring `extends`; standalone root MUST NOT declare it.
- Structural targeting, not document-wide selectors: `remove.root` = optional top-level fields by name; `remove.<mapName>` = named keys of keyed maps `workspaces`/`storage`; `remove.<arrayName>` = inherited array entries by that array's defined identity keys.
- Identity keys: `context[].id` (optional, preferred when present), `plugins.agents[].name`, object keys for `workspaces`/`storage`.
- MUST NOT use arbitrary field-combination matching or AST-wide selector matching; each removable array/map MUST define own deterministic identity model.
- Required top-level fields such as `schema` MUST NOT be removable.

### Schema reference
- `schema` REQUIRED. Only one schema active per project; per-workspace schema selection NOT supported.
- Prefix conventions: `@specd/schema-std` npm package → `node_modules/@specd/schema-std/schema.yaml`, version via npm `package.json`; `#spec-driven` → `default` workspace `schemasPath`; bare `spec-driven` = same as bare/`#name` = `#default:name` → `default` workspace `schemas` section; `#billing:my-billing-schema` → `workspaces.billing.schemas.fs.path/my-schema/schema.yaml`; relative `./schemas/custom/schema.yaml` → direct path resolved from dir containing `specd.yaml`; absolute path → direct.
- No implicit multi-level fallback; prefix determines exactly where lookup happens. `SchemaRegistry.resolve()` receives full value and dispatches on prefix.
- Resolution timing: command dispatch time, immediately before command body. Skipped by `--help`, `--version`, `init`, `config validate`, `plugin` subcommands.
- Error types: `ConfigValidationError` (malformed `specd.yaml`) and `SchemaNotFoundError`/`SchemaValidationError` (resolution failures) are domain errors in `@specd/core`, extend `SpecdError`, distinct types/messages/exit codes — config errors point at `specd.yaml` itself, schema errors at referenced schema.

### Invalidation policy
- Optional root `invalidationPolicy`: `none|surgical|downstream|global` — project default seeding new changes and resolving effective policy when change not overridden.

### Workspaces
- `workspaces` key REQUIRED, ≥1 entry, defining spec location, code location, local schema storage, ownership.
- `default` reserved = local project workspace; every config MUST contain it; `specd init` creates it if `workspaces` absent.
- `root` reserved for code-graph project-global resources; declaring workspace named `root` MUST raise `ConfigValidationError` at startup.
- Fields: `prefix` (optional logical path prefix), `specs` (REQUIRED), `schemas` (optional), `codeRoot`, `ownership`, plus optional graph/context filtering.
- `specs` (REQUIRED) — own `adapter` + adapter-specific config; only `"fs"` supported in v1. `specs.adapter.config.path` REQUIRED for fs; relative paths resolve from dir containing `specd.yaml`; may point outside project repo root, then application layer sets `RepositoryConfig.isExternal` `true`.
- `specs.adapter.config.metadataPath` (OPTIONAL for fs) — dir for `metadata.yaml`, mirroring spec capability path structure; relative resolves from config dir; when declared, config loader MUST resolve to absolute and retain on workspace specs adapter binding; kernel composition MUST prefer retained value wiring `SpecRepository`. Absent → auto-derivation from VCS root of `specs.adapter.config.path` + `/.specd/metadata/` (or `.specd/metadata/` relative to specs path parent when no VCS) is kernel-composition responsibility, NOT done by `config-loader.load()`.
- `schemas` (OPTIONAL) — own independent `adapter`/config for named local schemas; used when `schema` references `#workspace:name` or bare/#-prefixed name targeting it. `default` ws omitted → `adapter:{type:fs,config:{path:.specd/schemas}}`; non-`default` omitted → no local schemas, any `#billing:name` ref yields `SchemaNotFoundError`.
- `codeRoot` — impl code dir; used by `CompileContext` to tell agent where to write code. `default` ws → project root (dir containing `specd.yaml`); non-`default` ws → REQUIRED, no default.
- `ownership` — `owned` (create/modify/archive changes; default `default` ws), `shared` (modifiable, external teams may too), `readOnly` (context only, changes cannot target; default non-`default` ws).

### Workspace-level graph config
- Optional per-workspace `graph` block: `respectGitignore` (default `true`), `allowedPaths` (glob-syntax relative to `codeRoot`), `excludePaths` (gitignore-syntax, `!` negation, relative to `codeRoot`).
- `allowedPaths` set → only matching files indexed for that ws.
- `respectGitignore: true` → `.gitignore` loaded hierarchically (git root → codeRoot → subdirs during walk), applied with ABSOLUTE priority: no `excludePaths` pattern can re-include a `.gitignore`-excluded file. `false` → gitignore not loaded, `excludePaths` sole ruleset.
- `excludePaths` unspecified → built-in defaults: `node_modules/`, `.git/`, `.specd/`, `dist/`, `build/`, `coverage/`, `.next/`, `.nuxt/`. Specified → REPLACES built-ins entirely, no merge (user takes full ownership).

### Storage configuration
- Optional `storage` key, project storage adapters; generic binding shape `adapter:{type,config}`; adapter-specific options in `config` (e.g. `type: fs`, `config.path: specd-sdd/changes`).
- `SpecdStorageConfig` exposes raw bindings `changesAdapter`, `draftsAdapter`, `discardedAdapter`, `archiveAdapter` (`SpecdAdapterBinding`) + derived absolute local staging `changesPath`, `draftsPath`, `discardedPath`, `archivePath`.
- Section and each binding OPTIONAL; omitted → `ConfigLoader` MUST default to `fs` relative to `specdPath`: `changes`→`<specdPath>/changes`, `drafts`→`<specdPath>/drafts`, `discarded`→`<specdPath>/discarded`, `archive`→`<specdPath>/archive`.

### Named storage adapters
- Workspace storage MAY select named adapter instead of built-in fs composition; adapter-specific config block passes through as adapter-owned config. Referencing adapter name absent from merged built-in + external storage registries MUST fail with clear error.

### Config path & derived dirs
- Optional top-level `specdPath` (workspace folder + derived temp/graph/storage artifacts); omitted → `.specd` relative to dir containing `specd.yaml`.
- In-memory `SpecdConfig`: `specdPath` (absolute data dir), `configPath` (absolute `<specdPath>/config`). Derived: `{specdPath}/graph` graph persistence root, `{specdPath}/tmp` scratch for graph/indexing, `{configPath}/tmp/change-locks` change lock files.
- Loader MUST verify physical existence of all resolved absolute dirs (`specdPath`, storage staging paths, workspace paths); any missing → `StorageDirectoryNotFoundError`.

### Template variables
- Archive patterns + hook commands contain `{{namespace.key}}` expanded at runtime by `TemplateExpander` against variable map. Unmatched token MUST be preserved unchanged in output + warning emitted identifying token; informational only, never halts processing.

### Schema plugins
- Optional `schemaPlugins` array; same ref conventions as `schema` (npm, workspace-qualified, bare, path). Resolved/applied as merge layers AFTER base schema's `extends` chain, in declaration order.
- Each referenced file MUST have `kind: schema-plugin`; resolving to `kind: schema` → startup `SchemaValidationError`; unresolvable → startup `SchemaNotFoundError`.

### Schema overrides
- Optional `schemaOverrides` inline block = merge operations applied AFTER all plugins; mirrors `SchemaOperations` from merge engine, same semantics as `mergeSchemaLayers` (see `core:schema-merge`).
- Operations `create`, `remove`, `set`, `append`, `prepend` all optional; validated structurally at startup (shape, valid operation keys). Semantic validation (e.g. removing non-existent entry) at schema resolution time.

### Context spec selection
- `contextIncludeSpecs`/`contextExcludeSpecs` at two levels: project-level (always applied) and workspace-level (only when that ws active).
- Workspace ACTIVE if ≥1 of its specs listed in current change's metadata; change records its spec set in metadata file. `CompileContext` resolves each spec's ws by matching path against declared `specs.adapter.config.path` (or `specs.fs.path`) — NOT fs scan at compile time, NOT CWD, NOT `codeRoot`. Change listing specs from both `default` and `billing` activates both ws simultaneously.
- Pattern syntax (project vs ws level): `*` all ws specs (ws level = `{self}:*` this ws); `workspace:*` all specs in named ws; `prefix/*` under `prefix/` in `default` (ws level = this ws); `workspace:prefix/*` under `prefix/` in named ws; `path/name` exact in `default`, no descendants; `workspace:path/name` exact in named ws, no descendants.
- `*` allowed only in 3 positions: alone, sole suffix after `workspace:` (e.g. `billing:*`), sole suffix after path prefix ending `/` (e.g. `_global/*`). Never mid-segment.
- Qualifier by level: project-level omitted qualifier = `default:`; ws-level omitted qualifier = this ws (inside `billing:`, `['auth/*']` = `billing:auth/*`, `['*']` = all billing specs).
- Defaults: project `contextIncludeSpecs` `['default:*']`, project `contextExcludeSpecs` `[]`; ws `contextIncludeSpecs` `['*']` (= `{workspace-name}:*`), ws `contextExcludeSpecs` `[]`.
- `CompileContext` order: (1) project `context` entries in declaration order first; (2) project include patterns; (3) project exclude patterns (remove from step-2 set); (4) ws include patterns from each active ws (ws declaration order, then pattern order); (5) ws exclude patterns same order; (6) all specs via `dependsOn` traversal from change's `specIds`, following `dependsOn` links (resolved `change.specDependsOn` → `.specd-metadata.yaml` → content extraction) transitively until no new specs. Step-6 specs NOT subject to excludes in steps 3/5 — declared dependency always included regardless of project/ws excludes.
- Dedupe/truncation: spec matched by earlier pattern wins; spec matched by multiple includes appears once at position of first matching pattern; step-6 spec already in steps 2–5 keeps earlier position. Step-1 `context` entries NOT part of spec collection, injected as-is, never deduplicated against specs. `.specd-metadata.yaml` format → `core:spec-metadata`.
- Unknown ws qualifier → startup warning only (tolerant for partial setups) but `specd config validate` MUST error (typo silently excludes specs = dangerous). Non-existent spec IDs silently skipped at compile time. Invalid pattern syntax = startup error. `config validate` additionally warns when any include/exclude pattern at any level matches no specs on disk (non-fatal).

### Context mode
- Optional top-level `contextMode`: `list` (spec IDs + source metadata only, no descriptions/content), `summary` (default; catalogue with spec ID, title, description, no full content), `full` (full content), `hybrid` (direct change specs in full when caller includes them, all others as summaries).
- Legacy `lazy` REMOVED — MUST NOT be accepted as alias/fallback for `hybrid`.
- Project-level only; MUST NOT appear inside workspace entries (startup validation rejects as unknown field). Omitted → `summary`.

### Project context instructions
- Optional `context` array injects project instructions before spec content. Entry = `{instruction}` | `{file}` | `{id,instruction}` | `{id,file}`. `id` optional, stable identity for inherited removal in layered resolution. File paths resolve relative to dir of active config file unless absolute.

### Approvals
- Optional `approvals` section, both gates default `false`, independent flags.
- `spec` (default `false`): when `true`, `ready` state cannot transition directly to `implementing`; must first enter `pending-spec-approval`, receive explicit approval (approver identity, reason, timestamp), then `spec-approved` → `implementing`. When `false`, `ready → implementing` free.
- `signoff` (default `false`): when `true`, `done` cannot transition directly to `archivable` (whether structural modifications or only additions); must enter `pending-signoff`, receive explicit sign-off, then `signed-off → archivable`. Sign-off record captures what reviewed — new, modified, removed specs. When `false`, `done → archivable` free.

### Logging
- Optional root `logging` section; if omitted, fall back to built-in defaults. `level` (optional) minimum log level, MUST include `trace`, `debug`, `info`, `warn`, `error`, `silent`; defaults `info`.

### LLM optimization
- Optional top-level `llmOptimizedContext` boolean, default `false`. `true` → specd may invoke LLM for richer output than deterministic extraction (richer `description`, structured `given`/`when`/`then` for free-form scenarios, more precise `dependsOn` suggestions). `false`/absent → deterministic processing only. Project-level opt-in (offline/air-gapped CI leaves `false`).

### Plugin declarations
- MUST include `plugins` section grouped by type; config loader MUST validate at load time via Zod schema; structural errors → `ConfigValidationError` before any command runs.
- Shape: `plugins: { agents?: Array<{ name: string; config?: Record<string, unknown> }> }`. `name` required, `config` optional. Unknown plugin types rejected at validation time.

### Config writer port
- `ConfigWriter` = application-layer port complementing read-only `ConfigLoader`; MUST define: `initProject(options: InitProjectOptions): Promise<InitProjectResult>` (create new `specd.yaml` with default content), `addPlugin(configPath: string, type: string, name: string, config?: Record<string, unknown>): Promise<void>`, `removePlugin(configPath: string, type: string, name: string): Promise<void>`, `listPlugins(configPath: string, type?: string): Promise<Array<{ name: string; config?: Record<string, unknown> }>>`.
- `addPlugin` params: absolute `configPath`, plugin `type` (e.g. `"agents"`), `name` (package name, e.g. `@specd/plugin-agent-claude`), optional `config`. MUST return `Promise<void>`, add to `plugins.<type>` array, MUST NOT duplicate existing entry.

### Startup validation
- MUST reject invalid cascade instructions before any command proceeds; MUST fail `ConfigValidationError` when: `remove` present without `extends`; `extends` value other than `true` or string path; `extends: <path>` points outside applicable config chain; `remove.root` deletes required field like `schema`; `remove.workspaces`/`remove.storage` names key absent from inherited base; array removal cannot resolve exactly one inherited target under that array's identity rules.
- Failures are domain-level config errors surfacing through normal `SpecdError`/`ConfigValidationError` path.

### Legacy configuration warnings
- Legacy-compatible parsing SHALL surface non-fatal advisory warnings (config shape/compatibility, not startup-blocking) via `SpecdConfig.warnings`, produced during load, preserved on resolved config, available to host bootstrap consumers without recomputing/reformatting.
- Legacy `workspaces.default.specs` adapter format → warning naming `'workspaces.default.specs'`; fully omitting `storage` key resolves with NO storage warnings.

### Project-level graph config
- Optional root `graph` section for project-global settings. `includePaths` optional globs (relative project root) for project-global files outside ws-owned graph identities (e.g. `docs/**`, `package.json`). `excludePaths` optional gitignore-syntax patterns applied globally.
- `includePaths`-discovered resources → reserved `root:` namespace ONLY when not already owned by a configured workspace `codeRoot`.
- `graph.excludePaths` applies to project-global AND workspace discovery; workspace-level filters MAY add restrictions but MUST NOT remove/override global exclusions.

## Constraints
- Every field in `specd.yaml` validated at load time by Zod schema.
- `privacy.mode` `hash` requires `salt` (config or environment) or validation SHALL fail.
- Unknown top-level fields rejected by strict Zod schema.
- Cascade validation failures → `ConfigValidationError`; legacy shapes → non-fatal `SpecdConfig.warnings`, never blocking.
